rule: Normalize audio to -14 LUFS.
Keep night scenes readable: dim the light but keep the subject clearly visible.
Split long sentences into two beats with a camera change.
example: beat 1 lasts 7.5s without a new idea

rule: Hold each caption until the next word starts.
Merge very short sentences; a beat should last at least ~1.5 s.
Avoid white objects filling the frame; lower exposure or change angle.
Captions: 1 to 3 words only.
Match the reference exposure: avoid white sets and large bright surfaces filling the frame.
Keep the camera always moving (push/orbit/handheld) like the reference.
Keep the main subject filling at least a third of the frame; move the camera closer.
example: beat 2: subject too small / off-frame (87% background)

rule: User: no on-screen words except spoken captions (signs/labels/counters removed; engine-enforced).
User: replace the hissy "tsh tsh" transition whoosh with a soft low whoom.
Cut every 1-2 seconds; one visual per phrase.
Show some of the blueprint room in most shots so the diorama look is preserved.
example: beat 3: blueprint room not visible, framing too tight

rule: Each beat must add an object, change a character mode, add an effect or change the camera.
Water must look real: reflective physical material, small ripples, partial see-through tint. Never a flat opaque coloured box.
example: cranberry v1: bog water was a mint-green slab

rule: Scatter many small items randomly with size and colour variation (instanced). Never lay them out in a regular grid.
example: cranberry v1: berries sat in a perfect 16x11 grid

rule: The first second must show the striking result of the story (e.g. the red sea of floating berries), not bare ground.
example: cranberry v1: hook frame showed only soil

rule: Aim every beat's camera at that beat's new object; people, machines and trucks must be in frame and must not block the subject or fill the frame.
example: cranberry v1: farmer, harvester and truck off-screen; v2 preview: truck filled the last frames, farmer showed his back

rule: Keep rims, dikes and low walls at 0.2 m or less so low and close cameras still see the subject.
example: cranberry v2 preview: 0.42 m dike hid the vines

rule: A high critic score does not prove natural graphics. Always look at one sheet and judge realism yourself before sending.
example: cranberry v1 scored 95 but looked artificial
